Create a detached dm-verity hash tree and root hash for a data image.

## Inputs

| Name    | Kind | Description                                                     |
| ------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `image` | file | Data image with a positive length divisible by data-block-size. |

## Parameters

| Name              | Default    | Description                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `size`            | `0`        | Hash-tree capacity in bytes. Zero allocates the required space, rounded up to 1 MiB. |
| `hash-algorithm`  | `"sha256"` | Digest algorithm supported by veritysetup and OpenSSL, such as sha256 or sha512.     |
| `data-block-size` | `4096`     | Data block size in bytes.                                                            |
| `hash-block-size` | `4096`     | Hash block size in bytes.                                                            |
| `salt`            | `""`       | Hexadecimal salt. Empty uses the SHA-256 digest of the data image.                   |

## Outputs

| Name        | Kind | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `hash-tree` | file | Detached dm-verity hash-tree image.                   |
| `root-hash` | file | Root hash as hexadecimal text, followed by a newline. |

## Execution

| Setting      | Value        |
| ------------ | ------------ |
| Environment  | Rugix Bakery |
| Source epoch | Consumed     |
| Output cache | Allowed      |

## Behavior

Create detached dm-verity authentication data for a filesystem or other data
image. The image must have a positive length divisible by `data-block-size`. The
rule verifies the generated hash tree before exporting `hash-tree` and
`root-hash`.

The default salt and verity superblock UUID derive from the data image's SHA-256
digest. `size = 0` allocates the required hash-tree capacity, rounded up to 1
MiB; an explicit size must fit the authentication data. Fixed inputs,
parameters, source epoch, and tooling produce identical output bytes.

A hash tree authenticates data only when a trusted boot component authenticates
its root hash. For example, embed `root-hash` in a signed UKI's command line.
Keep the data image and hash tree together throughout assembly and updates. Use
`core/append-verity` to package both in one artifact with exported hash offset
and data-length metadata.

## Example

For example, protect an existing SquashFS image:

```toml
uses = "core/dm-verity"
inputs.image = { path = "system.squashfs" }
parameters.hash-algorithm = "sha256"
```

Save the invocation as `build-rule.toml` and run
`./run-bakery bake rule build-rule.toml build/result`. Outputs appear as
`build/result/hash-tree` and `build/result/root-hash`.
